challenge.reason: The old decision says secrets are never written to .faff/ and are read from environment variables only. Caching resolved API keys in .faff/cache/credentials.json writes literal secrets to disk under .faff/, which is the exact thing the old decision forbids. Being gitignored only prevents commits; it does not stop the plaintext file being read by other processes, swept into backups, copied into worktrees or containers, or uploaded with .faff/ artifacts. The why does not engage the old decision's rationale at all, and the claimed benefit is small: process.env reads are in-memory, and an in-process cache would give the same saving with no file. The supersession argument is unsound.
